l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Abstract
s: The unit concerns automatically inducing high-quality knowledge graphs from document collections through advances in slot filling. It presents a zero-shot slot-filling approach that extends dense passage retrieval with hard negatives and robust training procedures for retrieval augmented generation models. The model improves passage retrieval and slot value generation on the T-REx and zsRE datasets, ranks first on the KILT leaderboard, and demonstrates domain adaptation on a new TACRED slot-filling variant.

l: Slot filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Abstract
s: Slot filling asks a system to fill a missing value for an entity query of the form [ENTITY, SLOT, ?] using evidence from relevant passages. The paper presents a novel zero-shot approach to this task.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Introduction
s: Slot filling is described as a sub-task of Knowledge Base Population (KBP). Its goal is to recognize a predetermined set of relations for an entity and use them to populate infobox-like structures. A system can do this by locating the entity in a corpus and gathering information about slot fillers from the surrounding context. A slot filling system processes and indexes documents before being prompted with an entity and relations.

l: Slot filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Introduction
s: Slot filling is a sub-task of Knowledge Base Population. It recognizes a predetermined set of relations for an entity and uses them to populate infobox-like structures.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: The unit concerns slot filling systems and introduces KGI (Knowledge Graph Induction), an end-to-end system using Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). KGI improves KILT performance on T-REx and zsRE, with gains of 38.24% and 21.25% KILT-F1, respectively, over previously submitted systems. The system uses hard negative mining to improve DPR context-encoder training and supports domain adaptation by indexing a new corpus with a pretrained DPR. The authors evaluate this approach on a zero/few-shot variant of TACRED and release KGI’s pretrained models and source code.

l: Slot filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Slot filling fills out an infobox for an entity, sometimes providing evidence text to explain predictions. The unit presents KGI as an end-to-end slot filling system and discusses its evaluation on KILT benchmarks and a zero/few-shot TACRED variant.

l: KGI, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: KGI (Knowledge Graph Induction) is a slot filling system based on advanced training strategies for Dense Passage Retrieval and Retrieval Augmented Generation. It improves KILT-F1 by 38.24% on T-REx and 21.25% on zsRE compared with previously submitted systems, and it supports domain adaptation and zero/few-shot slot filling.

l: KILT, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: KILT standardizes the zsRE and T-REx zero-shot slot filling tasks and provides an evaluation framework for slot filling. The unit reports that KGI achieves large gains over previously submitted systems on these benchmarks.

l: zsRE, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: zsRE is one of the two zero-shot slot filling tasks standardized by KILT. KGI improves performance on zsRE by 21.25% KILT-F1 compared with previously submitted systems.

l: T-REx, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: T-REx is one of the two zero-shot slot filling tasks standardized by KILT. KGI improves performance on T-REx by 38.24% KILT-F1 compared with previously submitted systems.

l: TACRED, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: TACRED is used as the basis for a variant introduced to evaluate zero-shot and few-shot slot filling for domain adaptation. The unit describes this benchmark as a new dataset variant released with the paper.

l: DPR, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) is used by KGI to retrieve passages for slot filling. KGI extends DPR training with hard negative mining and uses a pretrained DPR to index a new corpus during domain adaptation.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is part of KGI’s end-to-end slot filling system. The unit states that limited retrieval performance affects the generation of the slot filler.

l: relation extraction, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Relation extraction is described as the weakest component in many pipelines for extracting relations between entities from text. The unit notes that rule-based, supervised, and distantly supervised approaches require substantial human effort.

l: hard negative mining, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Hard negative mining is incorporated into KGI’s DPR training strategy. The unit highlights its importance for training the context encoder when combined with end-to-end training for slot filling.

l: domain adaptation, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Domain adaptation in KGI consists of indexing a new corpus with a pretrained DPR and replacing the original Wikipedia index. This enables zero-shot slot filling for a new schema, while providing a few examples for each relation quickly improves performance in a few-shot setup.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling
s: This unit reviews language-model and retrieval-based approaches to zero-shot slot filling, including RAG, KILT, DPR, Multi-task DPR, DensePhrases, and GENRE. KILT's strongest baseline for producing slot fillers is RAG, which uses DPR to retrieve passages and a BART-initialized generator to produce answers, although its retrieval metrics are worse than BM25. Multi-task DPR improves retrieval by training DPR encoders on multiple KILT tasks. Knowledge Graph Induction (KGI) combines DPR and RAG, training both for slot filling in two phases using KILT provenance ground truth and target tail entities.

l: Slot filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling
s: Zero-shot slot filling is presented as a task enabled by pre-trained transformers and language models used as sources of knowledge. Retrieval-augmented systems such as RAG and REALM can provide textual provenance for generated slot fillers.

l: RAG, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling
s: RAG first uses DPR to gather evidence passages and then uses a BART-initialized sequence-to-sequence model to generate an answer from each passage concatenated with the query. In the KILT baseline, only the query encoder and generation component are fine-tuned, while the passage encoder trained on Natural Questions remains fixed. RAG performs best among the tested baselines for producing slot fillers, but its retrieval performance is worse than BM25.

l: KILT, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling
s: KILT introduced baseline approaches for its benchmarks, with RAG performing best among them for producing slot fillers. Its provenance ground truth is used to train the DPR model in Knowledge Graph Induction.

l: DPR, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling
s: DPR is used by RAG to retrieve evidence passages before answer generation. In Knowledge Graph Induction, both the DPR query encoder and passage encoder are trained using KILT provenance ground truth, and the query encoder is further trained during generation using the target tail entity as the objective.

l: Multi-task DPR, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling
s: Multi-task DPR trains the DPR passage and query encoders using multiple tasks from the KILT suite of benchmarks. Its top three retrieved passages are combined with the query and given to a BART model to produce the answer, resulting in large gains in retrieval performance.

l: KGI, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling
s: Knowledge Graph Induction is presented as an approach to zero-shot slot filling that combines a DPR model and a RAG model, both trained for slot filling. It uses a two-phase training procedure: first training DPR with KILT provenance ground truth, then training sequence-to-sequence generation and further training the query encoder using the target tail entity.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: The unit describes DPR training and hard negative mining as used by Karpukhin et al. (2020) and Multi-DPR (Maillard et al., 2021). Anserini retrieves candidate passages with BM25, and a remaining top-ranked passage becomes a hard negative for each query. DPR trains separate BERT-based query and passage encoders using positive passages, hard negatives, and batch negatives, with a row-wise softmax and negative log-likelihood loss. The trained passage encoder produces vectors for approximately 32 million KILT passages, which are indexed with HNSW in FAISS using 8-bit scalar quantization.

l: DPR, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: DPR uses keyword-based hard negative mining and trains query and passage encoders with positive passages, hard negatives, and batch negatives. Its trained passage encoder is used to generate vectors for approximately 32 million passages from the KILT knowledge source.

l: hard negative mining, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Hard negative mining uses Anserini to retrieve top-ranked passages with BM25 from a query made from the head entity and relation. Passages overlapping the ground-truth paragraphs or containing a correct answer are excluded, and the remaining top-ranked result is used as a hard negative.

l: hard negatives, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: A hard negative is the remaining top-ranked Anserini result after passages overlapping the ground truth or containing a correct answer have been excluded. It is paired with a query and its positive passage in DPR training.

l: query, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: A query consists of a head entity and relation, represented in the diagram in the form "head [SEP] relation." The query is encoded independently and compared by inner product with all passages in the batch.

l: positive passage, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: A positive passage is the passage given by the KILT ground-truth provenance. It is paired with a query and a hard negative in DPR training and is the target of the negative log-likelihood loss.

l: negative passage, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: A negative passage is a passage that is not the positive passage for a given query. The hard negative and the passages associated with other queries in the batch serve as negatives during training.

l: passage, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Passages are first indexed with Anserini and retrieved using BM25. After training, approximately 32 million passages from the KILT knowledge source are encoded as vectors and indexed for retrieval.

l: batch negatives, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Batch negatives are the positive and hard negative passages belonging to other queries in the same training batch. They are included among the negatives for each query.

l: DPR training data, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: DPR training data consists of triples containing a query, a positive passage given by KILT ground-truth provenance, and a hard negative passage.

l: passage encoder, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: The passage encoder is a BERT model that independently encodes passages. After training, it generates vectors for approximately 32 million passages in the KILT knowledge source.

l: query encoder, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: The query encoder is a BERT model that independently encodes queries. Its outputs are compared with passage representations using inner products.

l: KILT, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: KILT provides the ground-truth provenance for positive passages and a knowledge source containing approximately 32 million passages used for vector generation.

l: approximate nearest neighbors, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Approximate nearest neighbors are used to index the passage vectors for retrieval. The unit identifies HNSW as the approximate nearest-neighbor data structure used through the FAISS library.

l: HNSW index, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: The HNSW index is an approximate nearest-neighbor data structure built with the open-source FAISS library. It indexes the passage vectors, which are reduced to 8-bit scalar quantization to lower memory usage.

l: passage vectors, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening
s: Passage vectors are generated by the trained DPR passage encoder for approximately 32 million KILT passages. They are indexed with HNSW using FAISS and 8-bit scalar quantization.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: This unit describes how the query encoder is trained for slot filling and then injected into RAG for Natural Questions, where it can be updated without disrupting generation. RAG retrieves five passages with an ANN index, combines their weighted BART predictions, and trains the query encoder through the passages’ impact on generating the correct tail entity. The unit introduces Dense Negative Sampling (DNS), which mines DPR hard negatives from a learned dense index rather than with BM25. DNS and subsequent RAG training improve retrieval, with DPRDNS+RAG achieving the best reported results on both T-REx and zsRE.

l: query encoder, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: The query encoder is trained for slot filling alongside the passage encoder and is later injected into the RAG model for Natural Questions. RAG training updates it through the effect of retrieval on generation without disrupting the quality of generation.

l: Slot filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: The slot filling task trains the DPR model specifically to retrieve passages for head-and-relation queries and to predict the ground truth tail entity.

l: RAG, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: RAG retrieves the top five relevant passages, concatenates each passage with the query, and uses a generator to predict the tail entity. It marginalizes weighted next-token distributions across passages and trains the query encoder through the passages’ contribution to the correct output.

l: DPR, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: DPR is used to train the query and passage encoders for retrieval. The unit compares DPR models trained with Natural Questions, BM25 hard negatives, and dense-index hard negatives, with further RAG training improving retrieval.

l: KILT, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: KILT provides the slot filling data used to further train DPR and evaluate retrieval on T-REx and zsRE. KILT-trained DPR models are also used to build the dense index for mining hard negatives.

l: RAG for Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: RAG for Slot Filling predicts a ground truth tail entity from a head-and-relation query. It retrieves passages with an ANN index and uses a generator whose weighted predictions are combined before beam search selects the tail entity.

l: FAISS index, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: The ANN index retrieves the top five passages according to the inner product between query and passage vectors. It is also used to mine hard negatives for Dense Negative Sampling from the learned dense vector index.

l: BARTLARGE, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: BART receives each retrieved passage concatenated with the query and produces token prediction logits. Its token distributions are weighted by retrieval scores and combined across passages to obtain the next-token distribution.

l: Dense Negative Sampling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: Dense Negative Sampling mines hard negatives by searching a learned dense vector index with ANN rather than locating negatives with BM25. DNS initially lowers T-REx retrieval performance relative to DPRBM25, but DNS followed by RAG training produces the best reported performance on T-REx and zsRE.

l: BM25, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: BM25 is used to locate hard negative passages for DPRBM25. Dense Negative Sampling differs from this approach by retrieving hard negatives from a learned dense vector index.

l: T-REx, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: T-REx is evaluated for retrieval using R-Prec and R@5. The reported scores are 74.34 for R-Prec and 82.89 for R@5 for DPRDNS+RAG, the best results among the listed approaches.

l: zsRE, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: zsRE is evaluated for retrieval using R-Prec and R@5. DPRDNS+RAG obtains 98.60 for R-Prec and 99.70 for R@5, the best reported results in the table.

l: DPRDNS, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: DPRDNS is the DPR model immediately after Dense Negative Sampling training. It reaches 42.62 R-Prec and 55.09 R@5 on T-REx and 97.53 R-Prec and 99.30 R@5 on zsRE before additional RAG training.

l: RAG training, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: RAG training provides weak supervision based on a passage’s impact on producing the correct answer rather than on ground truth provenance. It substantially improves retrieval after DPR or DNS training, especially when applied to DPRDNS.

l: DNS training, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: DNS training is performed for two additional epochs using hard negatives retrieved from the learned dense index. It is the only training applied to the context encoder when negatives are drawn from the dense vector index.

l: hard negatives, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: Hard negatives are passages used for additional DPR training. In the DNS setting, they are mined by ANN search over a learned dense vector index instead of by BM25.

l: retrieval, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, opening .. Dense Negative Sampling
s: Retrieval performance is measured with R-Prec and R@5 on T-REx and zsRE. The results show large gains from RAG training after DPR, and the strongest overall scores from combining DNS with RAG training.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: This unit describes KILT experiments evaluating zero-shot slot filling on T-REx and zsRE. It explains passage segmentation of the KILT knowledge source, training settings for DPR, RAG, and the KGI systems, and their computational requirements. The evaluation compares retrieval methods and reports slot-filler accuracy, F1, provenance quality, and combined KILT metrics. KGI1 outperforms earlier systems, particularly on slot-filler accuracy and metrics requiring correct provenance.

l: KILT, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: KILT provides the knowledge source, provenance annotations, and evaluation framework used for the slot filling experiments. Its combined KILT-Accuracy and KILT-F1 metrics count slot-filler performance only when the correct provenance is provided.

l: T-REx, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: T-REx is much larger than zsRE in number of instances, although their training sets contain similar numbers of distinct relations. The experiments use only the first 500,000 T-REx training instances, and KGI1 substantially improves performance on T-REx.

l: zsRE, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: zsRE is one of the two zero-shot slot filling datasets evaluated in KILT. DPR training on zsRE takes about two hours on one NVIDIA V100 GPU, while RAG training on 147,000 zsRE instances takes about 15 hours on one NVIDIA P100 GPU.

l: Slot filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: Slot filling is evaluated using answer accuracy and token-level F1, with partial credit allowed for overlapping answer tokens. The experiments also assess whether systems provide the evidence supporting their generated slot fillers.

l: KILT knowledge source, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: The KILT knowledge source is a 2019/08/01 Wikipedia snapshot whose documents are segmented into passages. Passages are aligned with paragraph boundaries when possible, with short paragraphs combined and overly long paragraphs truncated.

l: Wikipedia, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: Wikipedia is used as the source of the KILT knowledge collection and as the default index distributed with Hugging Face for the RAG-KKS experiment. Generating a Wikipedia page title may be effective for retrieval because many relations for an entity are mentioned on its corresponding page.

l: RAG, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: RAG uses retrieved passages for sequence-to-sequence generation and has a default of five passages per query in these experiments. The study evaluates RAG with its default Wikipedia index, BM25 retrieval, and a Natural Questions-trained DPR retriever.

l: DPR, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: DPR is trained with a learning rate of 5e-5, batch size 128, two epochs, and a linear learning schedule. The experiments use BM25 hard negatives for KGI0 and dynamic negative sampling for KGI1.

l: KGI, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: KGI is based on RAG and contains BERTBASE query and passage encoders plus a BARTLARGE generator, totaling 620 million parameters. Its models are trained using the KILT data and provide both generated answers and provenance.

l: KGI0, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: KGI0 uses DPR trained with hard negative samples from BM25. On the development sets, it achieves higher retrieval and slot-filling performance than the RAG baselines on both zsRE and T-REx.

l: KGI1, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: KGI1 extends KGI0 by training DPR with dynamic negative sampling. It achieves the strongest reported development performance among the listed KGI systems and produces large gains over previous systems in slot-filling accuracy and combined KILT metrics.

l: retrieval, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: Retrieval is measured with R-Precision and Recall@5 against KILT provenance ground truth. The experiments compare the default RAG index, BM25, a Natural Questions-trained DPR retriever, and the KGI retrieval methods.

l: ground truth provenance, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: Provenance identifies the passages supporting a slot-filling answer and is evaluated against KILT ground truth. Systems other than RAG-KKS provide provenance for their top answer, and correct provenance is required for the combined KILT metrics.

l: slot fillers, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: The slot filler is evaluated with accuracy and token-level F1, where partial token overlap receives partial credit. KILT-Accuracy and KILT-F1 evaluate the slot filler only when the system also supplies the correct provenance.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Analysis .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: The unit evaluates retrieval and knowledge use in slot filling, comparing KGI1, KGI0, BARTLARGE, and other systems on KILT, zsRE, and T-REx. KGI1 performs best with gold passages but worst with random passages, showing that it uses explicit knowledge effectively while relying less on implicit knowledge. The analysis finds that explicit knowledge helps most for relations such as performer, author, and place of birth, while taxonomy and language relations are often handled by the language model. The unit then studies domain adaptation from Wikipedia and Wikidata-based tasks to TACRED, where KGI1 outperforms ranking baselines in zero-shot and improves further with few-shot training.

l: retrieval, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Analysis .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: Retrieval is evaluated using random, retrieved, and gold passages. Gold retrieval substantially improves accuracy, while random retrieval reduces performance for all systems.

l: KGI1, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Analysis .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: KGI1 is the strongest system for generating slot fillers from relevant explicit knowledge and achieves the best results on the reported KILT and T-REx evaluations. It performs worst with random passages, indicating that it has traded some implicit-knowledge capability for better use of explicit knowledge. In TACRED, it outperforms the ranking baselines in zero-shot evaluation and improves with one or four examples per relation.

l: BARTLARGE, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Analysis .. Slot Filling Evaluation

l: T-REx, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Analysis .. Slot Filling Evaluation
s: T-REx is used to evaluate slot-filling accuracy and to analyze how explicit knowledge affects different relations and entity-frequency groups. KGI1 substantially outperforms BARTLARGE on T-REx, while the gain from explicit knowledge shows no consistent dependence on entity frequency.

s: Explicit knowledge improves slot filling, especially for relations that are not central to an entity's meaning or predictable from surface features. s: Implicit knowledge is encoded in the language model and can support relations such as taxonomy, partonomy, and languages spoken, written, or signed. KGI1 sacrifices some implicit-knowledge performance in exchange for stronger use of explicit knowledge.

s: Few-shot learning is tested by fine-tuning KGI1 with one or four randomly selected training examples for each TACRED relation. HIT@1 improves by approximately five and ten percentage points, respectively, compared with the zero-shot result.

l: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling, Conclusion
s: The paper presents KGI, a novel approach to zero-shot slot filling that improves Dense Passage Retrieval with hard negatives from the dense index and uses robust training procedures for Retrieval Augmented Generation. The authors also proposed and released a zero/few-shot slot filling benchmark based on TACRED for evaluating domain adaptation, where KGI achieved much better zero-shot results than the baselines. KGI also showed significant improvements after rapid few-shot fine-tuning.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Abstract
s: The paper introduces multilingual keyphrase generation, a setting for automatically predicting keyphrases in languages beyond English. It contributes two datasets, EcommerceMKP and AcademicMKP, covering six languages. Its retrieval-augmented method uses a cross-lingual dense passage retrieval module to find relevant English passages whose keyphrase annotations support generation in low-resource languages. A retriever-generator iterative training algorithm mines pseudo parallel passage pairs to strengthen the cross-lingual passage retriever, and experiments show that the approach outperforms all baselines.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: The introduction concerns multilingual keyphrase generation, a task that predicts keyphrases for long texts and has been studied primarily on English datasets. The authors propose a retrieval-augmented method that uses related English passages and keyphrases to support generation in lower-resource languages. They also introduce retriever-generator iterative training to mine pseudo-parallel data and report improvements across experiments on both datasets.

l: keyphrases, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: Keyphrases are single- or multi-word lexical units that summarize text and support indexing, categorizing, and mining. In the proposed multilingual method, English keyphrases retrieved from related passages serve as hints for generating keyphrases in another language.

s: Keyphrase generation automatically predicts keyphrases for a piece of long text. Existing work has focused mostly on English datasets, while this unit investigates generation in multiple other languages.

l: multilingual keyphrase generation, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: Multilingual keyphrase generation is presented as an important but under-explored problem, partly because search engines serve users in different languages. l: English, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: English provides large-scale keyphrase resources that can be used as an external knowledge base for multilingual keyphrase generation. Related English passages and their keyphrases are retrieved to provide hints for generating keyphrases in lower-resource languages.

l: EcommerceMKP, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: EcommerceMKP is a multilingual keyphrase dataset collected from a major real-world e-commerce website. It uses product descriptions as source texts and user search queries as target keyphrases, containing 73,000 examples in Spanish, German, Italian, and French.

l: AcademicMKP, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: AcademicMKP is a multilingual keyphrase dataset in the academic domain. It contains 2,693 Chinese and Korean papers, using titles and abstracts as source texts and author-provided keyphrases as targets.

l: retriever-generator iterative training, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: Retriever-generator iterative training automatically mines pseudo training parallel pairs from unlabeled data to address the scarcity of parallel passage-keyphrase pairs. l: retrieval-augmented keyphrase generation, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: Retrieval-augmented keyphrase generation retrieves related English passages for a passage written in another language and uses their English keyphrases as hints. l: English datasets, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: English datasets are described as large-scale resources containing useful keyphrase knowledge. Experiments show that they can provide beneficial external knowledge for multilingual keyphrase generation.

l: multilingual keyphrase generation datasets, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Introduction
s: The unit states that no large-scale publicly available dataset existed for training and benchmarking multilingual keyphrase generation. It addresses this gap by introducing EcommerceMKP and AcademicMKP, which cover six languages and two domains.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Related Work
s: This unit reviews neural keyphrase generation and Retrieval Augmented Text Generation (RAG). It explains that English passage-keyphrase training data can serve as external knowledge for keyphrase generation, while prior retrieval methods do not generalize well to multilingual settings because of vocabulary gaps. The RAMKG framework uses Cross-Lingual Dense Passage Retrieval to find relevant English passages and their keyphrases for multilingual keyphrase generation with code-mixed inputs.

l: Keyphrase Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Related Work
s: Keyphrase generation uses neural language generation to produce keyphrases based on phrase importance and semantics rather than extracting substrings. l: CopyRNN, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Related Work
s: CopyRNN, proposed by Meng et al. (2017), generates words from a vocabulary and points to words in the source text. It addresses the difficulty of predicting keyphrases that are absent from the source text.

l: Retrieval Augmented Text Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Related Work
s: Retrieval Augmented Text Generation combines non-parametric knowledge retrieved by a sparse or dense retriever with parametric knowledge learned during pre-training. l: EcommerceMKP-EN, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Related Work
s: The English passage-keyphrase training data is treated as external knowledge for keyphrase generation. A retriever searches it for relevant English passages and associated keyphrases.

l: RAMKG, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Related Work

s: Multilingual keyphrase generation is described as a resource-scarce task, especially because non-English text and domain-specific keyphrase annotations are limited. The proposed framework uses retrieved English keyphrases as external knowledge when generating keyphrases in another language.

s: The retrieval-augmented approach uses relatively rich English resources to support multilingual keyphrase generation. l: RAMKG, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Model .. 4.3
s: The Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generator combines cross-lingual passage retrieval with multilingual keyphrase generation. It takes a source passage and retrieved English keyphrases as code-mixed input and generates keyphrases in the source language.

s: Cross-lingual dense passage retrieval encodes English passages offline and converts a non-English source passage into a query vector for nearest-neighbor search. s: Retriever-generator iterative training alternates between training a retriever, training a retrieval-augmented generator, and mining pseudo-parallel passage pairs. l: mBART, Retrieval-Augmented Multilingual Keyphrase Generation with Retriever-Generator Iterative Training, Model .. 4.3
s: mBART is used as the multilingual denoising sequence-to-sequence model for keyphrase generation. It receives retrieved English keyphrases and a source passage separated by special tokens, and it generates a target-language sequence of keyphrases.

s: It contains 2,693 manually checked scientific-paper examples in Chinese and Korean. Paper titles and abstracts are used as source text, and author-provided keywords are used as target output.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding / Abstract
s: The work, titled "Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding," concerns improving knowledge-intensive generation by incorporating answer information into retrieval-augmented generation. Wenyu Huang, Mirella Lapata, Pavlos Vougiouklis, Nikos Papasarantopoulos, and Jeff Z. Pan propose Dense Knowledge Similarity (DKS) and Retriever as Answer Classifier (RAC) to retrieve passages that are relevant to both questions and answers. They evaluate the approach on open domain question answering using MSMARCO and on conversation using Wizard of Wikipedia. The best models improve retrieval and generation metrics over a baseline, including Recall@1 and BLEU-4 on MSMARCO and R-Precision and KILT-RL on the KILT-WoW leaderboard.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: The unit introduces Knowledge-Intensive Generation (KIG), which uses external knowledge sources to generate responses and addresses hallucination in Large Language Models. It explains that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves passages before generating answers, but conventional training favors label-relevant passages over other knowledge-relevant passages. The proposed framework adds Retriever as Answer Classifier (RAC) and Dense Knowledge Similarity (DKS), using rich answer encoding to train retrievers to identify knowledge-relevant passages. Experiments on MSMARCO and Wizard of Wikipedia through the KILT benchmark report improvements in retrieval and generation performance over RAG.

l: Knowledge-Intensive Generation, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Knowledge-Intensive Generation consists of tasks that require external knowledge sources, such as passage corpora or knowledge graphs, to generate natural language responses to questions.

l: external knowledge sources, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: External knowledge sources support Knowledge-Intensive Generation and include passage corpora and knowledge graphs.

l: large language models, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Large Language Models such as GPT-4 can still produce plausible-looking statements that are factually incorrect when they lack external knowledge.

l: hallucination problem, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Hallucination is identified as a problem in which generated statements appear plausible but are factually incorrect.

l: RAG, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: RAG uses a retrieve-generate architecture: it first retrieves question-relevant passages and then generates responses based on them. In the example, RAG favors the label-relevant passage and fails to retrieve another knowledge-relevant passage.

l: retriever, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: A high-quality retriever is essential for Knowledge-Intensive Generation and can help verify and correct factual errors produced by Large Language Models. The proposed objectives train retrievers to recall more knowledge-relevant passages and improve their generalization.

l: reference answer, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: The reference answer for the question about the definition of tactful states that tactful describes someone or something showing regard for other people’s feelings. Existing training methods use token matches with reference answers to guide retriever and generator training.

l: knowledge-relevant passages, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Knowledge-relevant passages contain knowledge expressed in the answer even when they do not closely match its wording. The proposed framework treats both passages in the tactful example as positive and aims to retrieve such passages more effectively.

l: label-relevant passages, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Label-relevant passages have high token overlap with the reference answer. Conventional RAG training prefers these passages, which can cause it to miss other knowledge-relevant passages and overfit retrieval to the training data.

l: Retriever as Answer Classifier, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Retriever as Answer Classifier is one of the proposed objectives. It uses answer encoding to determine whether a retrieved passage contains the knowledge in the answer, making both example passages positive.

l: Dense Knowledge Similarity, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Dense Knowledge Similarity is one of the proposed objectives and compares answer and passage encodings in a knowledge representation space. It is designed to place knowledge-relevant passages closer to the answer than other passages.

l: Rich Answer Encoding, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: Answer encoding represents the knowledge contained in an answer and supports both Retriever as Answer Classifier and Dense Knowledge Similarity. It shifts training from token-level matching toward sequence- or knowledge-level matching.

l: MSMARCO, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding, Introduction
s: MSMARCO is used to evaluate the framework on generative question answering. The best model achieves a reported 12.1% relative improvement in Recall@1 and a 4.5% relative improvement in BLEU-4 over RAG.
